corrections.summary: NGINX Open Source: update to 1.30.8 or later on the stable branch, or 1.31.10 or later on the mainline branch. Those 23 Nov 2026 releases also fix CVE-2026-132779. Each CVE's affected range is the range on its own nginx.org row, including 0.6.18 through 1.31.8 for CVE-2026-123634. NGINX Plus version numbers were removed until a Plus release that also covers CVE-2026-132779 is confirmed from F5. 1Password is Act soon: the investigation began 19 Nov 2026, the disclosed copy includes Secure Remote Password parameters, private-repository source code, and CI/CD access, and the vendor's customer steps are listed one by one. Airbyte: rotate environment variables that were made available to the platform, and use the vendor's per-image times and remediation steps. Check Point: Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator R82.10 Take 36 or later, R82 Take 118 or later, and R81.20 Take 158 or later. vm2: update to 3.12.1 or later. Other update actions now say or later. KEV membership and EPSS were recorded for every CVE.
Items now record a kind. 1Password is an incident and Airbyte Core is a supply-chain compromise. Checks that did not change the customer action are labeled verification notes.

Added Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS (CVE-2026-46300, exploited and in KEV) as Act now, the Todoist security incident as Act soon with Todoist's customer steps, and an unverified early signal on a reported Rackspace Spot breach and shutdown.

Formatting only: the long actions for Palo Alto PAN-OS, Todoist, Check Point, Airbyte now show a short action followed by the vendor's steps as a numbered list. The advice and versions did not change.

Added three early signals from the 2 PM social scan: an unpatched Cacti remote code execution report, an unverified extortion claim against USA TODAY Co. subscribers, and a reported Zodia Custody data breach.

6 PM PT social scan: added Flight Centre Travel Group's booking-system incident (Act soon, from its ASX statement) and Canonical LXD CVE-2026-135384 (Act soon, update to 5.0.12, 5.21.10 or 6.10.2 or later), plus an early signal for a reported pre-authentication flaw in the Linux kernel NFS server that is not yet verified.

10 PM PT full run: added Mitel OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager CVE-2026-137724, CVE-2026-137721 and CVE-2026-137723 (Act soon, upgrade to V11 R2.14 or later) and the EasyEquities security incident (Act soon, from its help-centre notice), plus an early signal for a reported SAP GitHub security incident that is not yet verified. The feed cache showed no changes to earlier items.

Linux kernel NFS server (NFS2ROOT) is now verified as CVE-2026-99362 from the kernel.org CVE record: Act now, install a kernel with the fix (5.10.275, 5.15.226, 6.1.193, 6.6.163, 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2 or later on your branch) and reboot, or restrict port 2049. The Cacti early signal now notes a security company's report of exploitation attempts against its honeypot, which is still unconfirmed; there is still no Cacti fix.

Cacti (4HTTP2ROOT / 4HTTP2SHELL): the Cacti project merged a security hardening commit for guest writes and user settings to its develop branch. There is still no release, advisory or CVE, so the item stays unverified and guest access should stay off.

items.product: F5 NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus
items.priority_reason: NGINX is a widely deployed web server, a national CERT reports active exploitation, and the EPSS score for CVE-2026-123007 is high.
items.affected: NGINX Open Source, from each nginx.org advisory row: CVE-2026-123007 affects 1.9.5 through 1.31.8 (not vulnerable in 1.30.7+ and 1.31.9+); CVE-2026-123633 affects 1.19.7 through 1.31.8 (not vulnerable in 1.30.7+ and 1.31.9+); CVE-2026-123634 affects 0.6.18 through 1.31.8 (not vulnerable in 1.30.7+ and 1.31.9+); CVE-2026-132779 affects 1.21.4 through 1.31.9 (not vulnerable in 1.30.8+ and 1.31.10+). CSA Singapore lists NGINX Plus 37.0.0 to before 37.0.8.1, 37.1.0 to before 37.3.0.1, and R34, R35, and R36 for CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633.
items.summary: CVE-2026-123007 is a heap buffer overflow in NGINX HTTP/2 flow control. CSA Singapore says an attacker could crash a worker, corrupt memory, or possibly execute code, and that this CVE is reportedly being actively exploited. CVE-2026-123633 is an HTTP/2 use-after-free in the worker process; CSA Singapore says it can cause a denial of service or possibly code execution. CVE-2026-123634 is a use-after-free when the resolver is used and the same name is resolved in subrequests. CVE-2026-132779 is excessive CPU use when ssl_early_data is enabled. nginx 1.30.8 and 1.31.10, released 23 Nov 2026, fix it. None of these four CVEs were in the CISA KEV catalog (catalogVersion 2026.11.25). CSA Singapore reports CVSS v3.1 8.1 for CVE-2026-123007 and CVE-2026-123633.
items.action: Upgrade NGINX Open Source to 1.30.8 or later on the stable branch, or to 1.31.10 or later on the mainline branch. Also update ingress controllers and container images that bundle NGINX. For NGINX Plus, install the fixed release F5 names for your branch in article K000163926.
items.gaps: F5 article K000163926 did not render, so no NGINX Plus version is named for CVE-2026-132779.

items.priority_reason: This is a confirmed supply-chain compromise that can leak database and cloud credentials.
items.affected: On November 25, 2026, Airbyte says platform images were compromised from the listed time until a clean build was republished between about 1:25 and 1:40 PM PT. A copy is safe if it was pulled before its tampered-from time or after 1:40 PM. airbyte/server from 10:36 AM at 2.5.0; airbyte/worker from 10:53 AM at 2.5.0; airbyte/bootloader, cron, connector-sidecar, and container-orchestrator from 10:35 AM at 2.5.0; airbyte/workload-api-server, workload-init-container, and workload-launcher from 10:36 AM at 2.5.0. Docker Hub pulls were stopped between 11:42 AM and 11:55 AM PT, and compromised images were replaced between 12:25 PM and 1:40 PM PT. Connectors: source-postgres from 7:03 AM at 3.8.12; destination-postgres from 10:40 AM at 3.0.24; destination-redshift from 10:46 AM at 4.0.13; destination-bigquery from 10:46 AM at 3.2.3; source-facebook-marketing from 10:43 AM at 6.1.12; source-mssql from 11:00 AM at 5.1.5; source-mysql from 11:01 AM at 3.53.10; destination-snowflake from 11:02 AM at 5.2.2; source-google-sheets from 11:04 AM at 0.13.2. Safe connector replacement tags were published between about 12:50 and 1:05 PM.

fixes.component: Airbyte platform images (server, worker, bootloader, cron, connector-sidecar, container-orchestrator, workload-api-server, workload-init-container, workload-launcher)

items.summary: Airbyte says compromised open-source Core images can send credentials configured for a connection to an external server, and that credentials for any connection that ran one of these versions should be treated as compromised and rotated. The exposure window is the vendor's per-image tampered-from time on November 25, 2026, through the clean republish between about 1:25 and 1:40 PM PT. Airbyte 2.6.0 is the recommended platform replacement and also includes the Java4Shell fix. There is no CVE.
items.action: Upgrade to 2.6.0 or later and rotate environment variables that were made available to the platform.
steps: Upgrade each affected connector to its replacement tag or any later one: source-postgres 3.8.13 or later, destination-postgres 3.0.26 or later, destination-redshift 4.0.14 or later, destination-bigquery 3.2.4 or later, source-facebook-marketing 6.1.13 or later, source-mssql 5.1.6 or later, source-mysql 3.53.11 or later, destination-snowflake 5.2.3 or later, and source-google-sheets 0.13.3 or later.
In the Airbyte UI, click Workspace settings, click Sources or Destinations, click the pencil icon on the affected connector, enter the safe image version or its digest, and click Submit.

If you mirror images in your own registry and the tampered version is there, replace it immediately: authenticate to your registry, pull the safe tag, retag it into your registry while keeping the airbyte/<name>:<tag> path, and push it.
Rotate the credentials the connector used in the source or destination itself, then enter the new credentials in Airbyte.
Review activity in those tools from the first sync on the tampered image until you rotated: sign-ins, queries, and data changes.
If you find a match, email security@airbyte.io.

items.priority_reason: CVE-2026-16232 is in the KEV catalog and is tied to a fresh intrusion campaign against firewall management servers that GreyNoise expects to continue.
items.affected: R77.30, R80, R80.10, R80.20, R80.30, R81, R81.10, R81.20, R82, and R82.10, when the management server is reachable from the internet and Trusted Clients (GUI clients) are unrestricted.
items.summary: Check Point article sk185169 describes CVE-2026-16232, an authentication bypass in Security Management Server and Multi-Domain Security Management during SmartConsole login, and says it is exploited in the wild. The article's solution is a Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator for R82.10 starting from Take 36, for R82 starting from Take 118, and for R81.20 starting from Take 158. GreyNoise reports intrusions at 22 or more organizations between 2026-10-17 and 2026-11-02 and expects the campaign to continue. CISA added CVE-2026-16232 to the KEV catalog on 2026-07-22.
items.action: Install the Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator for R82.10 starting from Take 36 or later, for R82 starting from Take 118 or later, and for R81.20 starting from Take 158 or later.
steps: Follow the security hardening steps in sk185169: use the security hardening guide.
Limit Trusted Clients so the type is not Any.
Restrict management access and implied rules to trusted addresses.
Investigate exposed management servers for compromise.

items.priority_reason: This is critical unauthenticated remote code execution on e-commerce sites, and exploitation is reported.
items.affected: VirtueMart 4.0.0 through 4.8.7.
items.summary: CVE-2026-133335 is an unauthenticated local file inclusion issue in VirtueMart for Joomla that can lead to remote code execution. VirtueMart 4.8.8 fixed this CVE. Release 4.8.10 also fixes a further issue that lets someone fake a paid order. Social posts say the Joomla CNA record marks the CVE exploited in the wild. The VirtueMart news page and the NVD page read for this edition do not confirm that, so exploitation stays reported. The CVE was not in the CISA KEV catalog at this check.
items.action: Upgrade VirtueMart to 4.8.10 or later. Release 4.8.8 fixed CVE-2026-133335; 4.8.10 also fixes an issue that lets someone fake a paid order.
items.gaps: The hotfix build VirtueMart offers for 4.0 and later was not named.

items.priority_reason: This is a critical flaw in a very widely installed WordPress plugin.
items.affected: WP Rocket before 3.24.2.
items.summary: CVE-2026-125812 is a path traversal issue in the WP Rocket WordPress plugin that can lead to remote code execution. Versions before 3.24.2 are affected. Patchstack says exploitation is expected. This edition did not establish that it is being exploited. The CVE was not in the CISA KEV catalog at this check.
items.action: Update WP Rocket to 3.24.2 or later.
items.gaps: The Patchstack page was not re-opened when the action was changed to say or later.

items.priority_reason: A patch is available for critical unauthenticated remote code execution, and this edition did not establish exploitation.
items.affected: HPE Networking Management Software (AirWave) 8.3.0.7 and below.
items.summary: HPE bulletin HPESBNW05186 fixes 23 issues in AirWave, including CVE-2026-133973, unauthenticated command injection in the web management interface, and CVE-2026-133971, an authentication bypass. AirWave 8.3.0.7 and below are affected. The fix is 8.3.0.8 or later. Exploitation was not established for either CVE, and neither was in the CISA KEV catalog at this check.
items.action: Update HPE AirWave to 8.3.0.8 or later.
items.gaps: The HPE support page was not used. This item follows the CSAF bulletin.

items.priority_reason: Anyone who can run sandboxed pipelines can take over the controller, and patches are available.
items.affected: Script Security 1436.v1082791135e4 and earlier; Pipeline: Groovy 4403.v471713a_cea_19 and earlier.
items.summary: The Jenkins plugin advisory of 2026-11-25 includes a Script Security sandbox bypass (CVE-2026-136835, SECURITY-4278) and a Pipeline: Groovy sandbox bypass (CVE-2026-136834, SECURITY-4152). NVD now publishes those CVE identifiers, confirming numbers that the 25 November briefing did not treat as verified. Other plugins in the advisory are listed there. Exploitation was not established for either CVE, and neither was in the CISA KEV catalog at this check.
items.action: Update Script Security to 1436.1438.v3dc5ef7d16f2 or a later release, and Pipeline: Groovy to 4403.4405.va_b_cdb_b_d0b_89f or a later release, and update the other affected plugins named in the 2026-11-25 advisory.
items.gaps: The 2026-11-25 Jenkins advisory was not re-opened when the action was changed to say or a later release.

items.priority_reason: This applies when the embedder allowlists the crypto builtin. It is not in the KEV catalog, and the EPSS probability is low.
items.affected: vm2 through 3.12.0, when the embedder allowlists the crypto builtin.
items.summary: CVE-2026-93604 affects the vm2 Node.js sandbox through 3.12.0 when the embedder allowlists the crypto builtin. GitHub advisory GHSA-x3v6-43hc-82mc lists affected versions through 3.12.0 and shows 3.12.1, and npm publishes 3.12.1. Exploitation was not established. The CVE was not in the CISA KEV catalog (catalogVersion 2026.11.25).
items.action: Update vm2 to 3.12.1 or later. Do not allowlist the crypto builtin for untrusted code.
items.gaps: GitHub advisory GHSA-x3v6-43hc-82mc shows 3.12.1 beside affected versions through 3.12.0. Its narrative still says no patched version was identified. npm publishes 3.12.1.

items.priority_reason: The PyJWT fix has been out since September, and only applications that mix HMAC and asymmetric algorithm families are exposed.
items.affected: PyJWT before 2.14.0, when the application accepts both HMAC and asymmetric algorithms.
items.summary: CVE-2026-102268 is a key-confusion issue in PyJWT when an application accepts both HMAC and asymmetric algorithms. PyJWT before 2.14.0 is affected, and NVD records the fix as 2.14.0. Exploitation was not established, and the CVE was not in the CISA KEV catalog at this check.
items.action: Update PyJWT to 2.14.0 or later where the application accepts both HMAC and asymmetric algorithms.
items.gaps: The PyJWT release page was not opened, and a Red Hat Ansible Automation Platform fix was not established.

items.priority_reason: This is critical remote code execution in widely used Office software, and updates are available.
items.affected: Office LTSC 2024, Office LTSC 2021, and Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise.
items.summary: CVE-2026-112732 is a double-free vulnerability in Microsoft Office Visio that allows remote code execution. Microsoft rates it Critical and released updates on 2026-11-24. Exploitation was not established, and the CVE was not in the CISA KEV catalog at this check.
items.action: Install Office LTSC 2024 build 16.0.17932.21140 or a later build on that branch, or Office LTSC 2021 build 16.0.14334.21048 or a later build on that branch. For Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise, install the build listed at https://aka.ms/OfficeSecurityReleases.
items.gaps: The Microsoft 365 Apps for Enterprise build was not listed in the MSRC API. The action points at the Office security releases page.

items.priority_reason: 1Password confirmed that an attacker copied account records for a subset of customers, including invitation and recovery tokens. 1Password says customers do not need to change the account, and the remaining customer step is to watch for phishing.
items.affected: A subset of 1Password customers. Copied records include names and email addresses; account and user identifiers, account creation and last sign-in times; public keys; Secure Remote Password protocol parameters; tokens in emailed links for invitations, provisioning, and account recovery; and other non-secret account metadata. The attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to CI/CD. Vaults, the items in them, the keys that protect the vaults, the account password, the Secret Key, account recovery keys, and the apps and browser extensions were not accessed.
items.summary: On November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee's corporate GitHub account. The actor used the account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded administrative data. The downloaded account records for a subset of users include names and email addresses; account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times; public keys, which are public by design; Secure Remote Password protocol parameters, which cannot be used to access the account; tokens present in emailed links for invitations, provisioning, and account recovery; and other non-secret account metadata such as version numeric identifiers and file numeric identifiers. The attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to the CI/CD system. 1Password says that source code is not customer data and contains no user secrets, that CI/CD contains infrastructure-related secrets, and that those credentials were rotated, with no impact to services, availability, or product security. Vaults and the items in them, the keys that protect the vaults, the account password, the Secret Key, account recovery keys, and the apps and browser extensions were not accessed. A small number of users with a provisioning-invite or account-recovery token were specifically notified. The token cannot access the account by itself; it works only together with an SSO sign-in or a code sent to the registered email address. 1Password expanded that code from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric digits. There is no CVE.
items.action: You do not need to update anything in your 1Password account. Be cautious about phishing attempts in the form of unexpected emails, texts, or calls that mention 1Password, invitations, or account recovery. 1Password will never ask for your account password or Secret Key. Only enter them in the official 1Password app or on the official website, and only when you opened the app or typed the address yourself. The Secret Key is only needed the first time you sign in on a new device or browser. Keep your Secret Key and account password safe. If you see something suspicious, tell 1Password at support@1password.com.

sources.label: 1Password update on the November 2026 security incident

items.priority_reason: Palo Alto Networks has observed exploitation of CVE-2026-46300 against PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet, and CISA lists the CVE in its KEV catalog.
items.affected: PAN-OS releases earlier than the fixed hotfix for each release line listed in Palo Alto Networks bulletin PAN-SA-2026-0015 (for example, 11.2.10 builds before 11.2.10-h19).
items.summary: CVE-2026-46300 (Fragnesia) is a Linux kernel local privilege-escalation flaw that Palo Alto Networks has fixed in PAN-OS. Palo Alto says observed exploitation targeted PAN-OS devices whose management interface is exposed to the internet, and that the only known way to exploit it first requires the PHP2Shell vulnerability through that interface. CISA added CVE-2026-46300 to the KEV catalog on 28 October 2026.
items.action: Follow Palo Alto Networks' guidance for your setup.
items.gaps: Only bulletin PAN-SA-2026-0015 was read; the CVE-2026-109618 (PHP2Shell) advisory and the PAN-OS release list were not opened, so whether a newer hotfix than each listed version exists was not confirmed. No CVSS score was recorded.
steps: If you already run a fixed PAN-OS release listed in the CVE-2026-109618 advisory, you are protected.

If your management interface is restricted to trusted internal IP addresses, upgrade to the fixed hotfix for your release (such as 10.2.18-h15, 11.1.16-h6, 11.2.16-h3, 12.1.10-h6 or 12.2.4-h3) or a later release on the same branch at your next maintenance interval.
If your management interface, or a dataplane interface with a management profile attached, is reachable from the internet, upgrade immediately and restrict access to trusted internal IP addresses.

items.priority_reason: Todoist confirmed that an attacker retrieved customer information on November 23, 2026, and affected customers have account-specific steps to take.
items.affected: About 6% of Todoist users (email addresses, older salted SHA1 password hashes, and account creation dates); about 0.003% (Todoist API and Slack integration tokens, with project, task, and comment data accessed for a smaller subset); about 0.001% (content resembling credentials found by targeted searches); and about 0.001% (connected Todoist for Outlook mailboxes: email subjects, sender information, the beginning of messages up to 255 characters, and attachment details). The attacker could also read source code; Todoist found no changes to application code.
items.summary: Todoist says that between November 22 and 23, an attacker used a stolen credential associated with its version control system to modify automated workflows in three repositories and obtain additional credentials, then took over an employee's work account and reached its cloud infrastructure. On November 23, 2026, the attacker gained unauthorized access to production systems and retrieved some customer information. Todoist says it blocked the access paths, revoked and replaced exposed internal credentials, protected affected accounts, and emailed affected customers. How the first credential was obtained has not been established. There is no CVE.
items.action: Follow the instructions in the email Todoist sent you; if you did not receive one, Todoist says there is nothing to do. Todoist's notification comes from no-reply@notify.todoist.com; watch for fake emails.
steps: If your password was disabled, reset it and choose a new password, not your old Todoist password or one you use elsewhere.
If you reused your Todoist password elsewhere, change it on those services too.
If your Slack integration was disconnected, reconnect it.
If you used the Todoist for Outlook add-in, reconnect it.
If you used a Todoist API token in scripts or services, update them with your new token.
If you stored API keys, access tokens, recovery phrases, or other credentials in Todoist content, revoke and replace them with the relevant service.
If your content included shared links that let anyone with the link access a file, restrict access or replace those links.

items.product: Flight Centre Travel Group (Travel Associates, Cruiseabout)
items.priority_reason: Flight Centre Travel Group says a significant number of customer records in a third-party accommodation booking system may have been accessed, a very small share with limited passport details, and warns customers to watch for scam messages about their bookings.
items.affected: Customers whose accommodation bookings were made in the third-party accommodation system used by Flight Centre brand, Travel Associates, Cruiseabout and some independent agents. Flight bookings and corporate travel bookings are not affected. Most accessed records comprise only customer names, some with basic travel information; a very small percentage is believed to include limited passport details, email addresses, phone numbers, birth dates, or in rare cases health or mobility information. No access to credit card, payment or bank account details has been identified.
items.summary: In a statement to the Australian Securities Exchange dated November 26, 2026, Flight Centre Travel Group said it is investigating unusual activity in a third-party accommodation booking system used by some of its leisure travel brands. Activity has only been detected in the accommodation system used by Flight Centre brand, Travel Associates, Cruiseabout and some independent agents. The company believes a significant number of customer records in the system may have been accessed by unknown persons, although it is not yet clear how many were extracted. Most records comprise only customer names, some with basic travel information; a very small percentage is believed to include limited passport details, email addresses, phone numbers, birth dates, or in rare cases health or mobility information. No access to credit card, payment or bank account details has been identified. The company is working with Mandiant, changed authentication keys and credentials, and will contact impacted customers. There is no CVE.
items.action: If you booked accommodation through Flight Centre, Travel Associates or Cruiseabout, be alert to unexpected emails, calls or messages about your bookings, and don't click links, open attachments or share personal information, passwords or payment details in response.
items.gaps: The statement does not give the date the activity began or was detected, or the number of affected customers; the investigation is ongoing.

sources.label: Flight Centre Travel Group statement to the ASX, November 26, 2026

items.priority_reason: CVE-2026-135384 lets a remote attacker holding any token signed by the configured identity provider authenticate to the LXD API, but only on LXD servers with OIDC login configured.
items.affected: Canonical LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10 and 6.10.2 with OIDC authentication configured.
items.summary: CVE-2026-135384 is an improper-authentication flaw in OIDC bearer token verification in Canonical LXD. NVD's description says a remote attacker holding a token signed by the configured identity provider can authenticate to the LXD API and gain unauthorized control or impersonate users by presenting tokens issued for other applications, ID tokens, or unverified email claims. LXD before 5.0.12, 5.21.10 and 6.10.2 is affected. Exploitation was not established, and the CVE was not in the CISA KEV catalog at this check.
items.action: Update LXD to 5.0.12, 5.21.10 or 6.10.2 or later on your release line, prioritizing servers with OIDC login enabled.
items.gaps: The NVD page was read through a search result because a direct fetch timed out; its CVSS score and authority were not captured, and FIRST EPSS had no score for this CVE on 2026-11-26. The LXD release notes were not opened to confirm newer security releases.

sources.label: FIRST EPSS, no score returned on 2026-11-26

items.priority_reason: Reports say a credential breach reached customer Kubernetes environments and that the service will close on December 8, 2026, but Rackspace's own notice was not confirmed in this edition.
items.affected: Not yet confirmed from Rackspace. Reports describe Rackspace Spot customers' Kubernetes environments.
items.summary: Not yet verified. Posts and news reports say Rackspace will permanently discontinue Rackspace Spot on December 8, 2026, following a security breach involving compromised credentials that reached customer Kubernetes environments. This edition has not confirmed the details from a Rackspace notice.
items.action: Check whether you run workloads on Rackspace Spot; watch for Rackspace's customer notice on the breach and the shutdown date.
items.gaps: Rackspace's own incident or shutdown notice was not found; the public Spot release notes read in search results did not mention it. Breach date, scope, and customer steps are unconfirmed.

items.priority_reason: A researcher reports an unauthenticated remote code execution chain in Cacti 1.2.31, the latest release, with no fix and public code; the Cacti project has not confirmed it in this edition.
items.affected: Reported to affect Cacti 1.2.31 with guest access enabled; not yet confirmed by the Cacti project.
items.summary: Not yet verified. A researcher disclosed a flaw named 4HTTP2ROOT in Cacti 1.2.31, the newest release, and a SecurityOnline report says it lets an unauthenticated visitor run commands on the Cacti server when guest access is turned on. The report says no CVE id or vendor fix exists yet and no attacks in the wild have been confirmed. Cacti servers often hold network device credentials. On 27 November a security company said on X that its Cacti honeypot recorded exploitation attempts within 14 hours of a public proof of concept; that claim has not been confirmed by a primary source. On 28 November (UTC) the Cacti project merged a security commit to its develop branch titled "harden user settings validation, Guest writes, and realtime graph access"; it is not in a release yet, and the project has not published an advisory or CVE tying it to this report.
items.action: Check whether you run Cacti and whether guest access is enabled and reachable; watch for an advisory from the Cacti project.
items.gaps: No Cacti project advisory, CVE record or release fix was found as of 28 November; the newest Cacti release is still 1.2.31. A security hardening commit was merged to the develop branch, but the project has not said it fixes this report. Affected versions and the guest-access mitigation come only from the researcher write-up as reported by SecurityOnline. Exploitation in the wild is unconfirmed; the only report of attempts is a vendor's post on X.

sources.label: SecurityOnline report on the researcher's disclosure
Cacti project commit on GitHub (develop branch), 28 November

items.priority_reason: An extortion group claims to hold about 166 million USA TODAY Co. subscriber records; the publisher has not confirmed a breach.
items.affected: Not confirmed. The claim describes USA TODAY Co. subscriber records.
items.summary: Not yet verified. Posts say the extortion group n0n listed USA TODAY Co. on its leak site, claiming theft of about 166 million subscriber records and about 27 million emails. The publisher has not confirmed a breach, and the claim is unverified.
items.action: If you have a USA TODAY or affiliated newspaper subscription, be wary of phishing that mentions your subscription; watch for a notice from the publisher.
items.gaps: No statement from USA TODAY Co. was found. Whether any data was taken, its date and its scope are unconfirmed; the figures are the group's claim as relayed in a post.

items.priority_reason: Reports say Zodia Custody confirmed an unauthorized party accessed limited client and staff contact details; Zodia's own notice was not read in this edition.
items.affected: Not yet confirmed from Zodia Custody. Reports describe institutional client and employee contact information.
items.summary: Not yet verified. Posts and news summaries say Zodia Custody, an institutional digital-asset custodian, detected probing on November 23, took its B2B API offline, and found that an unauthorized party had accessed limited information such as contact names and emails for a small number of clients and staff. Reports say no unauthorized transactions occurred and service has been restored.
items.action: If your organization is a Zodia Custody client, check for a notice from Zodia and watch for targeted phishing using your contacts' names.
items.gaps: Zodia Custody's own statement was not read; dates, scope and the no-transactions claim come from posts and news summaries.

items.priority_reason: Unauthenticated remote kernel memory corruption in the NFS server, CVSS 9.8 from kernel.org, with upstream fixed releases available. Hosts that do not run an NFS server are not affected.
items.affected: Linux kernel NFS server (nfsd) from 3.16 before 5.10.275, 5.15.226, 6.1.193, 6.6.163, 6.12.117, 6.18.61 and 7.3.2 on those branches, per the kernel.org CVE record. Hosts that do not run an NFS server are not exposed.
items.summary: CVE-2026-99362, which researchers call NFS2ROOT, is a flaw in the Linux kernel NFS server's session reply handling that lets a remote, unauthenticated client write past a kernel buffer. kernel.org scores it CVSS 3.1 9.8. It has been present since kernel 3.16 and is fixed upstream on every supported branch. Exploitation was not established, and it was not in the CISA KEV catalog at this check. This is the same flaw as the linux-nfsd item in the 25 November edition.
items.action: Install a kernel that includes the fix (5.10.275, 5.15.226, 6.1.193, 6.6.163, 6.12.117, 6.18.61, 7.3.2 or later on your branch, or a distribution kernel that names CVE-2026-99362) and reboot. Until then, stop nfs-server if you do not need it, or restrict TCP port 2049 to trusted networks.
items.gaps: Distribution kernel versions were not checked in this run; the mitigation wording follows the 25 November linux-nfsd item, which cited Red Hat.

items.priority_reason: CVE-2026-137724 and CVE-2026-137721 let an unauthenticated network attacker gain access to or run commands on OpenScape 4000 systems (CVSS 10.0 from Mitel), but exploitation was not established and none of the three CVEs was in CISA KEV at this check.
items.affected: Per Mitel advisory MISA-2026-0013: OpenScape 4000 V11 R0.22 through V11 R2.11, and V10 R1.68 and earlier; OpenScape 4000 Manager V11 R0.22 through V11 R2.11, and V10 R1.34, V10 R1.42, V10 R1.54 and V10 R1.68. The CVE records list each product as affected from V11 R0.22 before V11 R2.14.
items.summary: Mitel advisory MISA-2026-0013 (first issued 2026-11-18) covers three critical flaws in the Platform component of OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager, which received CVE ids on November 27, 2026 (UTC): CVE-2026-137724, an unauthenticated unauthorized-access flaw (CVSS 3.1 10.0); CVE-2026-137721, an unauthenticated command injection (CVSS 3.1 10.0); and CVE-2026-137723, a command injection reachable by an unauthenticated attacker with adjacent network access (CVSS 3.1 9.6). A successful attack could expose sensitive information or run arbitrary commands on the system. Exploitation was not established, and none of the three is in the CISA KEV catalog.
items.action: Upgrade OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager to V11 R2.14 or later; on V11 R1.26 apply PLT HF5, and on V10 R0.28 to V11 R0.22 (Manager: V10 R1.34 to V11 R0.22) apply Mitel's patch.
steps: Upgrade OpenScape 4000 and OpenScape 4000 Manager to V11 R2.14 or a later release.
On V11 R1.26, apply the PLT HF5 hotfix, or upgrade to a later release.
On OpenScape 4000 V10 R0.28 to V11 R0.22, or OpenScape 4000 Manager V10 R1.34 to V11 R0.22, apply the patch Mitel provides for those releases.
If you cannot update in time, enable Security Mode restricted access as Mitel's workaround, following Mitel knowledge base article KB000129263.
items.gaps: Mitel's advisory still lists only its internal ids MTLVULN-1785, MTLVULN-1786 and MTLVULN-1793; the CVE mapping (137724 to 1785, 137721 to 1786, 137723 to 1793) is inferred from the matching descriptions and CVSS vectors in the CVE records, which link to the advisory. The CVE records list only V11 R0.22 before V11 R2.14 as affected, while the advisory also lists V10 releases. Mitel's release list and knowledge base article KB000129263 were not opened to confirm a newer security release. FIRST EPSS returned no score for these CVEs on 2026-11-27.

sources.label: FIRST EPSS, no score returned on 2026-11-27

items.priority_reason: EasyEquities says a security incident is affecting some of its systems, has taken client login offline, and is still assessing whether personal information was accessed, while warning clients about scam contact.
items.affected: EasyEquities clients. Client login and some services are restricted for all client accounts, including child accounts managed by a guardian. EasyEquities is still assessing whether any personal information was accessed; it says all client funds are accounted for and secure based on its investigation to date.
items.summary: South African investment platform EasyEquities, owned by Purple Group, says that on 26 November 2026 it emailed every client about a security incident affecting some of its systems, which it is investigating with independent specialists. As a precaution it restricted client login and some services, and it is keeping the platform offline while it completes checks. In a later update it said all client funds are accounted for and secure based on its investigation to date, and that it is assessing whether any personal information may have been accessed. It says the incident is not related to the September 2026 incident at a third-party service provider. There is no CVE.
items.action: If you have an EasyEquities account, treat any unexpected call, email, SMS or WhatsApp asking for personal or banking details with caution even if it seems to come from EasyEquities, and never share your password or one-time PIN.
steps: Don't keep trying to log in; EasyEquities will announce by email and on its social channels when access is back.
Treat unexpected calls, emails, SMS or WhatsApp messages asking for personal or banking details with caution, even if they seem to come from EasyEquities.
Never share your password or one-time PIN, and don't change banking details or approve a payment because someone asked without checking with EasyEquities first.
If you see anything on your account you didn't do, or suspect fraud, email fraud@easyequities.co.za.
items.gaps: EasyEquities has not said when the incident was detected, which systems were affected, how access was gained, or whether personal information was accessed; the investigation is ongoing. The later update on client funds and the September incident comes from TechCentral's report of EasyEquities' statement.

sources.label: EasyEquities Help Centre: Security Incident November 2026

items.priority_reason: SAP says it identified suspicious activity and took protective measures, and reports say attackers used stolen employee GitHub tokens to copy and alter SAP source code; SAP has not confirmed that or said whether any customer software was affected.
items.affected: Not yet confirmed by SAP. Reports describe SAP's GitHub platform for developer productivity and software delivery; SAP says it has found no evidence so far of unauthorized access to customers' business data.
items.summary: Not yet verified. SAP said in a statement to the press on Thursday evening, November 26, that it had identified suspicious activity and immediately took the necessary measures to protect its customers, and that it has found no evidence so far of unauthorized access to customers' business data. Der Spiegel, citing an insider, reported that attackers stole SAP employees' GitHub authentication tokens and used them to copy and alter SAP source code; Handelsblatt reported that SAP restricted GitHub access, paused automated build and delivery pipelines and rotated code-signing keys. SAP has not confirmed those details or said which repositories were affected, or whether any altered code reached customer software.
items.action: If you run SAP software or use SAP's open-source projects, watch for SAP guidance on affected repositories, builds or code-signing keys before trusting new SAP-signed packages.
items.gaps: No SAP advisory or customer notice was found; SAP's statement was read only as quoted in news reports (read through search excerpts). The token theft, source-code changes, affected repositories, and any effect on shipped builds or signing keys are unconfirmed.

gaps: Verification notes on individual items record checks that did not change the customer action, including the F5 NGINX Plus article that did not render.
